Nit only: tests/test_console.py:299 uses skipif(sys.platform == "win32") with reason "legacy windows is not tested here". That skips the test on all of Windows, not just legacy Windows, and the reason text is slightly inaccurate. The reference instead returns early when console.legacy_windows is set, and the neighbouring test_show_cursor has no skip. This reduces Windows coverage but is not a repository-convention violation, so it is not a failure.
The feature sets the window title on Console and Control and handles legacy Windows. control.py:33 writes the OSC 0 sequence \x1b]0;{title}\x07, the same bytes the reference test expects.
console.py:1154-1169 returns True only when the control was written, and the docstring says the title may not actually change. This matches the reference's documented caveat.

Behaviour matches the reference. Neither sanitises control characters from the title, and both write nothing when Console.control skips a dumb terminal (console.py:1510 in base). These are shared properties, not regressions from the original, so they are not counted as deficiencies.
